name: OT agreement structure
what: "An OT is a type of contracting instrument that is not a [procurement contract](#term:grant), grant, or cooperative agreement." [1385](#cite:1385) For DoD OTs the [FAR](#term:far), [DFARS](#term:dfars), DoD Source Selection Procedures and CICA do not apply (p. 19), and "OTs are not subject to the [Contract Disputes Act](#term:contract-disputes-act)." [1049](#cite:1049) The terms live in the agreement itself: a posted prototype OT has 16 articles: scope; term and termination; project management; agreement administration; performance objectives and changes; inspection/acceptance; financial matters; report and data requirements; confidential information; IP rights; [data rights](#term:sbir-data-rights); regulatory rights; foreign access to data; publications; human subjects; miscellaneous [1414](#cite:1414).
applies_when: Whenever the award instrument is an other transaction, whether signed directly with an agency or reached through a consortium. A January 2026 government training deck lists agencies with OT authority, including DoD, DHS, NIST, NOAA, NIH, NHLBI, NCATS, CDC, BARDA, NSF, ARPA-H, DOE, FAA, TSA, DOT, PHMSA, DNI and NASA [1388](#cite:1388).
steps: Does not apply (training slide 26): CICA, Truthful [Cost or Pricing Data](#term:certified-cost-or-pricing-data) Act, [Cost Accounting Standards](#term:cost-accounting-standards), Contract Disputes Act, procurement [protest](#term:bid-protest) process, FAR and supplements, Bayh-Dole (35 U.S.C. 202-204), [Service Contract Act](#term:service-contract-act), [Buy American Act](#term:buy-american) (in part) [1388](#cite:1388)

Still applies (training slide 25): Antideficiency Act, False Claims Act, false statements, Civil Rights Act, environmental statutes, [debarment](#term:responsibility) and suspension, research misconduct, human subjects and animal welfare rules [1388](#cite:1388)
Prototype OTs are Federal agency procurements for Procurement Integrity Act purposes (p. 15) [1049](#cite:1049)

Agreement terms the DoD guide discusses (II.E.3): price reasonableness, IP, physical property, disclosure and security, modifications, disputes, termination, follow-on production, recovery of funds, Government access, [Comptroller General](#term:gao) access, [flow-down](#term:flow-down), accounting systems [1049](#cite:1049)
"Modifications of ongoing prototype and production OT projects are common." [1049](#cite:1049)
Termination, in one posted agreement: for convenience on at least 30 days' written notice; cure period 10 business days [1414](#cite:1414)
Disputes, in one posted agreement: written request to the OTAO; "OTAO will review the matter and render a decision in writing within sixty (60) calendar days."; then court or ADR [1414](#cite:1414)

IP, in one executed [base agreement](#term:base-agreement): the awardee retains ownership of subject inventions and the Government gets a nonexclusive, irrevocable, paid-up license (Art. 9.1); data rights are unlimited for data produced exclusively with Government funds, government purpose rights for cost-shared data, limited rights for trade secrets (Art. 8) [1377](#cite:1377)

IP at civilian agencies: [ARPA-H](#term:arpa-h) typically seeks a license, not ownership, in inventions [1385](#cite:1385); "[NSF](#term:agency-abbreviations) will generally not apply the provisions of Bayh-Dole to OA/Ts" [1404](#cite:1404)
Property under [research OTs](#term:research-ot): the Government generally should not take title to property except deliverables (3.J.1) [1410](#cite:1410)
Follow-on production may be awarded without competition if competitive procedures were used for the prototype and it was successfully completed [1029](#cite:1029)
Administration: "Administration for OTs may only be performed using support agreements." [1416](#cite:1416)

Foreign access: one executed base agreement requires notice to HHS before transferring technology to foreign firms (Art. 10.2) [1377](#cite:1377); the DoD guide mentions [export controls](#term:export-controls) only as a limit on foreign participation (p. 12) [1049](#cite:1049)

Civilian guides: FAA OTAs "are not generally subject to AMS policy and regulations" [1102](#cite:1102); all DOE OT agreements go through Office of Acquisition Management business clearance and Senior Procurement Executive approval [1093](#cite:1093); NSF may form OTs only for the Directorate for Technology, Innovation, and Partnerships [1404](#cite:1404)

name: OT payable milestones and cost share
what: [OT](#term:other-transaction) payment comes in two families: fixed, with "Payments not based upon amounts generated from the Performer's financial / cost records", and expenditure-based (training slides 115-120) [1388](#cite:1388). The DoD guide covers [payable milestones](#term:payable-milestone) (III.M.1, p. 31) and advance payments (III.M.2) [1049](#cite:1049). For a DoD [prototype OT](#term:prototype-ot), at least one third of total cost from non-Federal sources is one of four alternative statutory conditions [1029](#cite:1029).
applies_when: When an OT sets payable milestones, and when the award relies on cost share. Under 10 U.S.C. 4022 subsection (d) the alternatives to the one-third share are (A) at least one nontraditional defense contractor or nonprofit research institution participating to a significant extent, (B) all significant participants being small businesses or nontraditional defense contractors, and (D) a senior procurement executive determination [1029](#cite:1029).
steps: Payment types: fixed price vs expenditure-based; fixed milestones vs expenditure-based milestones (slides 115-120) [1388](#cite:1388)

32 [CFR](#term:cfr) Part 3 defines [fixed-price](#term:firm-fixed-price) agreements as "Agreements where payments are not based on amounts generated from the awardee's financial or cost records."; [cost-type](#term:cost-reimbursement-contract) includes agreements that require [one-third cost share](#term:cost-share) by statute [1037](#cite:1037)
[NIH](#term:agency-abbreviations): "There are three primary payable milestone options available for OTs: fixed, adjustable (cost reimbursable), and a hybrid approach" [1099](#cite:1099)
FAA: payment structures named are milestones, advance payments, cost-reimbursable (V.A) [1102](#cite:1102)

Advance payments: "Both OT statutes allow for advance payments" [1049](#cite:1049); the [research OT](#term:research-ot) authority may be exercised without regard to 31 [U.S.C.](#term:usc) 3324 [1031](#cite:1031); advances beyond need are kept in an interest-bearing account, interest returned (3.I.1) [1410](#cite:1410)
[BARDA](#term:barda): "The Secretary may use milestone-based awards and payments" [1369](#cite:1369)

DoD prototype cost share (III.L, p. 29): at least one-third when that condition is relied on; may include labor, materials, equipment, IP rights, facilities, IR&D; not forgone fee or profit, nor cost of money; not costs incurred before the agreement's effective date [1049](#cite:1049)

Pre-agreement costs count as cost share only on a written agreements-officer determination (32 CFR § 3.6) [1037](#cite:1037); the statute excludes them unless an official determines in writing they were incurred in anticipation [1029](#cite:1029)

DoD research OT: Government funds "do not exceed the total amount provided by other parties to the [cooperative agreement](#term:grant) or other transaction", to the extent the Secretary determines practicable [1031](#cite:1031); resource share to the maximum extent practicable 50/50 (2.D.4.a) [1410](#cite:1410)

What counts (research OT guide 2.D.4.b): cash (labor, benefits, overhead, materials, IR&D) and in-kind (equipment, facilities, materials, IP); does not count: forgone profit or fee, previously Government-funded research, IR&D before award, cost of money [1410](#cite:1410)
"Burden of proof is on the Proposer/Performer" (training slide 85) [1388](#cite:1388)

Civilian examples: DOE, 50% cost share is the standard under 42 U.S.C. 7256(g) [1093](#cite:1093); [ARPA-E](#term:arpa-e) SCALEUP Ready, at least 33.3%, or 20% for small businesses [1357](#cite:1357); BARDA EZ-BAA, respondent contributions a minimum of 30-50% of total proposed project value [1366](#cite:1366); NASA Tipping Point 2023, "at least 10-25%, based on company size" [1344](#cite:1344); [ARPA-H](#term:arpa-h), cost sharing not generally required [1385](#cite:1385); NIH, optional unless the program's legislation says otherwise [1099](#cite:1099)

[Consortia](#term:consortium) test this per project: NAC [solicitations](#term:solicitation) require nontraditional participation or 1/3 cost share on each proposed effort [1169](#cite:1169); in one RRPV solicitation cost sharing is strongly encouraged, not required, and fee is allowed when cost share is not proposed [1376](#cite:1376)
A [consortium manager](#term:consortium-manager)'s page puts research OTA cost share at typically 50/50, negotiable [1425](#cite:1425)

conflicts: No DCAA page on OT audits was found; the audit rules here rest on 32 CFR Part 3 and the DoD OT Guide [1037](#cite:1037) [1049](#cite:1049).
32 CFR Part 3 still cites 10 U.S.C. 2371, the old numbering [1037](#cite:1037).
name: OT financial systems and audit access
what: [Cost Accounting Standards](#term:cost-accounting-standards) are among the rules that do not apply to [OTs](#term:other-transaction) (training slide 26) [1388](#cite:1388). For expenditure-based payment the DoD guide says the performer should have a system capable of complying with GAAP (p. 25) [1049](#cite:1049). Audit is negotiable except as [10 U.S.C. 4022](#term:prototype-ot) and 32 [C.F.R.](#term:cfr) 3.8 require (III.K, p. 28) [1049](#cite:1049).
applies_when: On any OT with payment tied to the firm's cost records or with cost share; the mandatory access clauses apply to DoD prototype OTs above $5,000,000 [1037](#cite:1037) [1029](#cite:1029).
steps: "Avoid imposing system requirement that cause the Performer to revise and/or add system(s)" [1388](#cite:1388)

"Avoid requirements that would force participants to use different financial management systems than they currently use in their ordinary course of business."; the financial system should follow recognized accounting principles such as GAAP (3.G) [1410](#cite:1410)

Fixed agreements: "Generally, fixed amount agreements should not require any type of audit provisions." [1049](#cite:1049); "In most cases, fixed support awards should not require any type of audit provision." [1410](#cite:1410); "DoD access to records is not generally required for [fixed-price](#term:firm-fixed-price) type OT agreements." [1037](#cite:1037)

32 CFR § 3.8: DoD access on [cost-type](#term:cost-reimbursement-contract) OTs with total Government payments over $5,000,000; [DCAA](#term:dcaa) or a qualified IPA for business units not under the Single Audit Act [1037](#cite:1037)

32 CFR § 3.7: [Comptroller General](#term:gao) access [clause](#term:clause-numbering) over $5,000,000; exception for entities with no audit-access agreement in the prior year; HCA waiver [1037](#cite:1037); the statute gives a three-year window after final payment [1029](#cite:1029)
Audit provisions flow to subawards, per the sweep's summary of 32 CFR Part 3 [1037](#cite:1037)

Worked examples: financial records open to Government audit and to GAO (RRPV [base agreement](#term:base-agreement) Art. 6.1) [1377](#cite:1377); records subject to audit for up to five years after expiration (MCDC base OTA Art. V.J) [1415](#cite:1415); data retained 7 years after completion in a posted prototype OT [1414](#cite:1414)

Civilian: [NIH](#term:agency-abbreviations) audits normally only when staff determine necessary (II.I) [1099](#cite:1099); NSF treats audit as negotiable, per the sweep's summary of its guide [1404](#cite:1404)

L.](#term:public-law) 119-106, the Stop Secret Spending Act of 2025 (enactment date as extracted by the fetch), amends the Federal Funding Accountability and Transparency Act so that [other transaction agreements](#term:other-transaction) are reported on [USAspending.gov](#term:usaspending): within 1 year a compilation report listing other transaction agreements; within 3 years "data relating to other transaction agreements is automatically transmitted to the website"; within 2 years, if not compliant, an implementation plan to Congress; [inspector general](#term:dod-ig) reports within 1 year and at least every 2 years for 10 years [1421](#cite:1421). [GAO](#term:gao) had found over $40 billion in OTAs not reported to USAspending.gov [1129](#cite:1129).

conflicts: PIEE/WAWF: the requirement comes from the DoD OT Guide and one posted agreement [1049](#cite:1049) [1414](#cite:1414); no PIEE page specific to OT invoicing was fetched, and the official URL given, piee.eb.mil, appeared in search results only and was not read.

FPDS help says only DoD and DHS can create OT records, so how NASA, HHS, DOE and others report is unverified; the FPDS help page may be legacy [1086](#cite:1086). How an OT record currently appears on USAspending.gov was not checked.
CPARS and OTs is verified only by absence [603](#cite:603) [985](#cite:985); no official sentence stating that CPARS does not cover OTs was found.
Five-year OT totals by department appear only in a sponsor's press release, a secondary source, and are not carried as fact [1422](#cite:1422).
name: OT payment and reporting (PIEE/WAWF, SAM, public reporting)
what: DoD OT invoicing runs through [WAWF](#term:wawf) in PIEE (III.M) [1049](#cite:1049). "Prior to being awarded an OT, the primary awardee must be fully registered for All Awards in [SAM](#term:sam-gov)" [1049](#cite:1049). Reporting frequency and type are set in the agreement, and little or none may be needed under fixed [payable milestones](#term:payable-milestone) (III.H, p. 27-28) [1049](#cite:1049).
applies_when: Before award, for registration, and after award, for invoicing and reports, on any OT [1049](#cite:1049).
steps: SAM: each [consortium member](#term:consortium) that is the primary performer needs a [UEI](#term:uei) (p. 26) [1049](#cite:1049); "All [ARPA-H](#term:arpa-h) [solicitations](#term:solicitation) require a valid UEI to submit a proposal." [1386](#cite:1386); SVIP needs a UEI in SAM.gov before award [1311](#cite:1311); [BARDA](#term:barda)'s EZ-BAA requires SAM registration before proposing [1366](#cite:1366)
Performer registration is generally required in the Government's procure-to-pay application (PMS, PIEE) [1388](#cite:1388)

Worked example, a posted [prototype OT](#term:prototype-ot): invoices through Wide Area Workflow, "2 in 1" document type; "Payments will be made within thirty (30) calendar days of receipt of a request for payment" (Art. 7.D) [1414](#cite:1414)
[DIU](#term:diu): payment by milestone through WAWF [95](#cite:95)
Under a consortium, invoices are emailed to the [consortium management firm](#term:consortium-manager) (RRPV [base agreement](#term:base-agreement) Art. 5.2) [1377](#cite:1377)
ARPA-H: "Funds are typically disbursed after the performer successfully completes milestones" [1386](#cite:1386)

Reports: may be tied to line items or milestones (III.H) [1049](#cite:1049); one posted agreement requires weekly teleconferences, quarterly progress reports within 20 days, monthly financial reports within 20 days and a draft final report by day 45 after project end [1414](#cite:1414); one base agreement requires quarterly/monthly, annual and final reports (Art. 4.3) [1377](#cite:1377); [DOE](#term:agency-abbreviations): "progress reports at least quarterly are recommended" [1093](#cite:1093); ARPA-H: "Reporting requirements are negotiated for each OT based on the needs of the program." [1385](#cite:1385)

Where the award is recorded: the Government reports prototype and [production OTs](#term:follow-on-production) to [FPDS](#term:fpds) and [research OTs](#term:research-ot) to FAADC (III.G) [1049](#cite:1049); FPDS help says "The only agencies that can access an OT are DoD and DHS." name: Consortium project agreement
what: Under a [consortium](#term:consortium) [OT](#term:other-transaction), "The [CMO](#term:consortium-manager), in turn, issues a [project sub-award](#term:base-agreement)—which executes the project—to the consortium member" [1119](#cite:1119). steps: Membership comes first: "Offerors must be RRPV Members to be eligible to submit a proposal" [1376](#cite:1376); at MTEC the prime offeror must be a member, needs a [UEI](#term:uei) and [CAGE code](#term:cage-code), and submits through BIDS [1424](#cite:1424)
SECONDARY ONLY: "Consortium membership does not guarantee an OT award!" [1426](#cite:1426)

The Government selects and directs: under one base OTA it issues a Technical Direction Letter to the CMF for each selected project (Art. I.C), and the CMF signs the OTA on behalf of the consortium (Art. III.C) [1415](#cite:1415)

[Flow-down](#term:flow-down): "The applicable provisions of the OTA have been incorporated by the CMF into this Agreement and any forthcoming Project Awards" [1377](#cite:1377); the base agreement "provides the terms and conditions that generally apply to all projects awarded and serves as a starting point for negotiations" [1119](#cite:1119)

IP is set before any project: "Intellectual Property (IP) rights for RRPV Project Awards will be defined in the terms of the RRPV Base Agreement" [1376](#cite:1376); under one base OTA the project agreement holder keeps title to patents and the Government takes a license (Art. X.B) [1415](#cite:1415)

Money: invoices are emailed to the CMF (Art. 5.2); payment methods include [fixed-price](#term:firm-fixed-price) milestones and expenditure-based [1377](#cite:1377); one RPP offers cost reimbursable milestones, [cost plus fixed fee](#term:cost-reimbursement-contract) milestones, fixed price milestones [1376](#cite:1376)
Disputes escalate to a level above the [BARDA](#term:barda) OTAO (Art. 16.1); financial records are open to Government audit and to [GAO](#term:gao) (Art. 6.1) [1377](#cite:1377)

Member-paid fees as posted: NAC, "There is a one-time $500 fee to join and no recurring annual member dues.", with an award assessment of 0.15% (AMTC) or 0.5% (DOTC and NEST) of awarded funding, not ceiling [1169](#cite:1169); NSTIC, no annual membership fee and an assessment of 0.05% of all awarded funding (not ceiling), effective October 1, 2025 [1194](#cite:1194); RRPV, "There are currently no membership dues." V.E) [1415](#cite:1415)

One membership can cover several OTAs: "We offer membership to NSTXL, which provides your firm access to all of our OTAs." [1141](#cite:1141)

Public data: "for consortia-based OTAs, the consortium management organization, rather than the awardees performing the work, is reflected in the [FPDS](#term:fpds) data" [1121](#cite:1121); in FPDS, if "Consortia" is Yes, the UEI of the primary consortia member is required [1086](#cite:1086); the [DoD IG](#term:dod-ig) found DoD "did not have an accurate count of OTs or the associated dollar values" [1417](#cite:1417)
